messages:
sana: Proposing a "quorum" gating pattern for the int4/v3 bring-up. Instead of single-metric auto-fallback, require concordance across multiple signal types (fidelity, MRR, latency tail) to trigger auto-fallback. Also add a human sanity-handoff if any metric exceeds an aggressive threshold.

kevin: makes sense. What quorum count do you want? 2/3? 3/3? :thinking_face:

sana: leaning 2/3. Rationale: tolerate single-signal noise but catch correlated regressions. Human ack if any metric hits the "hard" thresholds.

jules: +1 to 2/3. We should also piggyback slice-weighting — a 10% weighted slice failing is worse than 3 isolated 1% slices.

maya: Agree on slice weighting. Also propose a "soft-fail" alarm that reduces traffic to the variant (to 5%) and runs extended shadow if quorum == 1 but absolute degradation on a heavy slice.

sana: good call. Draft config idea:

```yaml
quorum_gate:
  metrics: ["mrr_delta", "fidelity_drop_pct", "p99_latency_ms"]
  thresholds:
    mrr_delta: -0.02        # fail if MRR drops more than 2%
    fidelity_drop_pct: 5    # fail if fidelity metric drops >5% (weighted)
    p99_latency_ms: 150     # fail if p99 latency >150ms
  require: 2               # need 2/3 failing to auto-fallback
  human_ack_threshold:
    mrr_delta: -0.05
    fidelity_drop_pct: 10
  auto_fallback: true
  soft_fail_action:
    reduce_traffic_pct: 5
    shadow_extend_minutes: 60
```

kevin: implementation note: rollout-service will need to emit `quorum_reason` tag and `failing_metric_list` so ops can triage quickly. Also add `slice_weight` in telemetry.

infra-bot: smoke-run results for run_id=98413:
```
canary_run 98413: samples=12k, slices={short:40%, longdoc:35%, rare:25%}
metrics:
  mrr_delta: -0.012
  fidelity_drop_pct: 6.0
  p99_latency_ms: 135
decision: quorum_fail_count=1/3 -> NO auto-fallback (require=2)
actions: alerted #eng-oncall, holding at 10% traffic, evaluating slice weights
```

deploy-bot: Canary started (id=98413) · promoted traffic -> 10% · owner=@sana

maya: fidelity_drop_pct=6 on longdoc slice is concerning even if quorum=1. Recommend reduce traffic to 5% and enable extended shadow for longdoc.

jules: if longdoc is 35% of impressions then that 6% weighted drop is material. I vote for soft-fail: reduce traffic + extend shadow.

kevin: I'll wire the soft-fail action into rollout-service and add a human-ack step: if any metric >= human_ack_threshold OR quorum_count==2 -> pause and require `@release-owner ack` in the rollout UI.

sana: thanks. Can we also make the policy pluggable per-model? Some models have higher tolerance for latency vs fidelity.

kevin: yeah, policy will be model-scoped with defaults. I'll add a config flag `require_human_for_serious=true` for enterprise customers.

infra-bot: follow-up from telemetry (t+20m) for run_id=98413:
```
longdoc slice: fidelity_drop=6.8%, samples=4200 (35% weighted)
short slice: fidelity_drop=0.4%, samples=4800
rare slice: fidelity_drop=0.9%, samples=3000
aggregate mrr_delta: -0.014, p99_latency: 138ms
quorum_fail_count=1 -> soft-fail triggered (reduce traffic to 5%, extended shadow 60m)
notifications: #eng-oncall, #product-notify, release-owner @maya
```

maya: acked the handoff. Will run focused evals on longdoc slices (prompt mix + long prefixes).

jules: doc note: we should capture this pattern as `quorum-with-softfail` in the gatebook and include a sample playbook entry for when longdoc weight >30%.

sana: filed a short runbook PR. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

kevin: I'll push the rollout-service PR with telemetry tags and a toggle for `soft_fail_action`. ETA EOD.

sana: leaving this open until we validate extended-shadow results. If the next run pushes quorum_fail_count to 2/3 we auto-fallback and create a postmortem.

deploy-bot: Canary update (id=98413): traffic reduced to 5% per soft-fail action.

infra-bot: final snapshot (t+90m): quorum_fail_count=1, longdoc fidelity now 5.2% (improved), mrr_delta -0.009, p99_latency 132ms. Canary remains at 5% shadow -> monitoring.

sana: closing for now — action items: kevin PR, jules gatebook entry, maya focused evals. Follow-up next retro.
